questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used. The Reynolds number R is a constant used in the study of liquids flowing through pipes. R is a pure number with no unit. ρvD R = µ where ρ is the density of the liquid, v is the speed of the liquid and D is the diameter of the pipe through which the liquid flows. What are the SI base units of µ?

options.A: kgms B kgm–1s C kgms–1 D kgm–1s–1

questions.questionText: Measurements are subject to systematic error and random error. Which measurements have high accuracy and low precision?

options.A: high random error and high systematic error
options.B: high random error and low systematic error
options.C: low random error and high systematic error
options.D: low random error and low systematic error

questions.questionText: The density of the material of a coil of thin wire is to be found. Which set of instruments could be used to do this most accurately?

options.A: metre rule, protractor, spring balance
options.B: micrometer, metre rule, top-pan balance
options.C: stopwatch, newton-meter, vernier calipers
options.D: tape measure, vernier calipers, lever balance

questions.questionText: A cylindrical tube rolling down a slope of inclinationθ moves a distance L in time T. The equation relating these quantities is    a2  L 3+ = QT2 sinθ  P    where a is the internal radius of the tube and P and Q are constants. Which row gives the correct units for P and for Q? P Q

options.A: m2 m2s–2
options.B: m2 ms–2
options.C: m2 m3s–2
options.D: m3 ms–2

questions.questionText: Variables x and y are related by the equation y = p – qx where p and q are constants. Values of x and y are measured experimentally. The results contain a systematic error. Which graph best represents these results?

options.A: B y y p p 0 0 0 x 0 x
options.C: D y y p p 0 0 0 x 0 x

questions.questionText: A cheetah and an antelope are 100m apart. The cheetah spots the antelope and runs towards it. The antelope reacts to the cheetah after one second and runs directly away from the cheetah. Both animals take 2 seconds to reach their top speeds. The graph shows how the speeds of the two animals vary with time. speed m s–1 30 cheetah
antelope 0 5 10 15 20 time / s How far apart are the animals, 17 seconds after the cheetah began running?

options.A: 4m B 11m C 54m D 89m

questions.questionText: A boy throws a stone with a horizontal velocity of 10ms–1 from the top of a building. The height of the building is 8.0m. The stone travels along a curved path until it hits the ground, as shown in the diagram.
m s–1 building 8.0 m ground How long does it take the stone to reach the ground? (Air resistance can be neglected.)
A rocket of mass 30000kg sits on a launch pad on the Earth’s surface. The rocket motors provide an upward force of 330kN on the rocket. What is the initial acceleration of the rocket?

Two equal masses X and Y are moving towards each other on a frictionless air track as shown. The masses make an elastic collision. air track 50cms–1 30cms–1 X Y Which row gives possible velocities for the two masses after the collision? velocity of X velocity of Y

options.A: zero 20cms–1 to the right
options.B: 10cms–1 to the right 10cms–1 to the right
options.C: 20cms–1 to the left zero
options.D: 30cms–1 to the left 50cms–1 to the right

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct with reference to perfectly elastic collisions between two bodies?

options.A: Neither total momentum nor total kinetic energy need be conserved but total energy must be conserved.
options.B: Total momentum and total energy are conserved but total kinetic energy may be changed into some other form of energy.
options.C: Total kinetic energy and total energy are both conserved but total momentum is conserved only if the two bodies have equal masses.
options.D: Total momentum, total kinetic energy and total energy are all conserved.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes a couple?

options.A: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in opposite directions which produce rotational motion but not translational motion
options.B: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in opposite directions which produce translational motion but not rotational motion
options.C: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in the same direction which produce rotational motion but not translational motion
options.D: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in the same direction which produce translational motion but not rotational motion

questions.questionText: A cross-shaped structure, freely pivoted at O, has arms of lengths 5.0m, 4.0m, 3.0m and 2.0m. It is acted on by forces of 2.0N, 3.0N, 4.0N and an unknown force F. The structure is in rotational equilibrium. F 5.0 m 2.0 N 2.0 m O 4.0 m 30° 3.0 N 3.0 m 4.0 N What is the magnitude of force F?
A trolley starts from rest at X. It rolls down to Y and eventually comes to rest at Z. X Z Y Which row is a possible summary of the energy changes during this process? X to Y Y to Z

options.A: p.e. → k.e. k.e. → p.e. key
options.B: p.e. → k.e. k.e. → p.e. + heat p.e. = potential energy
options.C: p.e. → k.e. + heat k.e. → p.e. k.e. = kinetic energy
options.D: p.e. → k.e. + heat k.e. → p.e. + heat

questions.questionText: An object of weight 15.0N is pulled along a horizontal surface at a constant velocity of 2.00ms–1. The force pulling the object is 12.0N at 30° to the horizontal, as shown. 2.00 m s–1 12.0 N 30° 15.0 N What is the power used to move the object?

Brownian motion can be demonstrated by illuminating smoke particles inside a closed, transparent container. When the particles are viewed using a microscope, bright specks of light are observed to move with constant, random motion. What cannot be inferred from this observation?

options.A: Air molecules are in constant motion.
options.B: Air molecules are in random motion.
options.C: Air pressure is due to air molecules colliding with the container.
options.D: The mass of an air molecule is much less than the mass of a smoke particle.

questions.questionText: A U-tube has one arm of area of cross-section A and the other of cross-section 4A. The tube contains water of density 1000kgm–3 and oil of density 850kgm–3, as shown. oil x 30.0 cm water The column of oil on top of the water in the left-hand arm is of length 30.0cm. What is the difference in height x between the levels in the two arms of the tube?

options.A: 4.5cm B 6.2cm C 23.8cm D 25.5cm stress

questions.questionText: The Young modulus of a metal may be determined from the ratio when the metal is strain stretched elastically. This can be done by making measurements when loads are added to a wire. Which measurements are needed to calculate the stress and strain of the wire in such an experiment? stress strain

options.A: wire diameter initial and final wire’s original mass added positions of load length
options.B: wire diameter mass added wire’s original initial and final length positions of load
options.C: wire’s original initial and final wire diameter mass added length positions of load
options.D: wire’s original mass added wire diameter initial and final length positions of load

questions.questionText: A copper wire of length 3.6m and diameter 1.22mm is stretched elastically by a force of 37N. The Young modulus of copper is 1.17 × 1011Pa. Which extension is caused by this force?

options.A: 0.24mm B 0.76mm C 0.97mm D 3.1mm

questions.questionText: When all the other features of a wave are constant, which relationship is correct?

options.A: Amplitude is directly proportional to velocity.
options.B: Intensity is directly proportional to amplitude.
options.C: Velocity is directly proportional to wavelength.
options.D: Wavelength is directly proportional to frequency.

questions.questionText: A vibrating rod makes a water wave in a ripple tank. The graph shows the displacement of the wave at one instant as it travels away from the rod. The wave speed is 2.0cms–1. displacement / mm distance / cm 0 0.4 0.8 1.2 –2 –4 What is the frequency of the wave?

options.A: 0.8Hz B 1.6Hz C 2.5Hz D 5.0Hz

questions.questionText: Polarisation is a phenomenon associated with a certain type of wave. Which condition must be fulfilled if a wave is to be polarised?

options.A: It must be a light wave.
options.B: It must be a longitudinal wave.
options.C: It must be a radio wave.
options.D: It must be a transverse wave.

questions.questionText: The following statements describe the diffraction of waves passing through a narrow slit. Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Both transverse and longitudinal waves can be diffracted.
options.B: Diffraction can only be seen with light when the light is monochromatic.
options.C: Red light diffracts through a greater angle than blue light.
options.D: The angle of diffraction increases when the width of the slit decreases.

questions.questionText: Monochromatic light is directed onto a pair of slits. Interference fringes that are 2.0mm apart are observed on a distant screen. The frequency of the light used is then doubled and the slit separation is halved. How far apart are the new interference fringes?

options.A: 0.50mm B 2.0mm C 4.0mm D 8.0mm

questions.questionText: A diffraction grating has N lines per unit length and is placed at 90° to monochromatic light of wavelength λ. What is the expression for θ, the angle to the normal to the grating at which the third order diffraction peak is observed?

Two parallel plates R and S are 2mm apart in a vacuum. An electron with charge –1.6 × 10–19C moves along a straight line in the electric field between the plates. The graph shows how the potential energy of the electron varies with its distance from plate R. +4.8 × 10–19 potential energy / J 0 1 2 distance / mm Which deduction is not correct?

options.A: The electric field between R and S is uniform.
options.B: The electric field strength is 3000NC–1.
options.C: The force on the electron is constant.
options.D: The magnitude of the potential difference between R and S is 3V.

questions.questionText: Two parallel, conducting plates with air between them are placed close to one another. The top plate is given a negative charge and the bottom one is earthed. Which diagram best represents the distribution of charges and the field between the plates?
In terms of energy transfer W and charge q, what are the definitions of potential difference (p.d.) and electromotive force (e.m.f.)? p.d. e.m.f. W W A q q W

options.B: Wq q W
options.C: Wq q
options.D: Wq Wq

questions.questionText: A cell of electromotive force E and internal resistance r is connected to an external resistor, as shown. E r I V The current in the circuit is I and the potential difference (p.d.) across the external resistor is V. In the equation (E – V) = Ir , what does the term (E – V) represent?

options.A: electrical energy per unit charge lost in the cell
options.B: electrical energy per unit charge lost in the complete circuit
options.C: electrical energy per unit charge lost in the connecting wire
options.D: electrical energy per unit charge lost in the external resistor

questions.questionText: Tensile strain may be measured by the change in electrical resistance of a device called a strain gauge. A strain gauge consists of folded fine metal wire mounted on a flexible insulating backing sheet. The strain gauge is firmly attached to the specimen. specimen strain gauge When the strain in the specimen is increased, what happens to the resistance of the wire?

options.A: It decreases, because the length decreases and the cross-sectional area increases.
options.B: It decreases, because the length increases and the cross-sectional area decreases.
options.C: It increases, because the length decreases and the cross-sectional area increases.
options.D: It increases, because the length increases and the cross-sectional area decreases.

questions.questionText: In the circuit shown, lamp P is rated 250V, 50W and lamp Q is rated 250V, 200W. The two lamps are connected in series to a 250V power supply. 250 V P Q Assume that the resistance of each lamp remains constant. Which statement most accurately describes what happens when the switch is closed?

options.A: Lamp P emits four times as much power as lamp Q.
options.B: Lamp P emits twice as much power as lamp Q.
options.C: Lamp Q emits four times as much power as lamp P.
options.D: Lamp Q emits twice as much power as lamp P.

questions.questionText: The cooling system in many houses is controlled by three electrical switches. These are: • a thermostat switch that closes when the temperature rises to a given value, • a clock switch that closes at times when cooling may be required, • an override switch that closes to turn on the system when exceptional temperature rises occur. Which diagram shows the switches correctly connected between the power supply and the cooling system? thermostat clock

options.A: power supply cooling system override thermostat
options.B: power supply cooling system override clock thermostat override clock
options.C: power supply cooling system thermostat override
options.D: power supply cooling system clock

questions.questionText: A 110V supply of negligible internal resistance is connected to a heater through a fuse and a switch. fuse switch C1 S+ 110 V heater S– C2 Terminals S+ and S– are the positive and negative terminals of the supply. Points C1 and C2 at either side of the heater are accessible for fault-finding.

options.A: a break in the wire of the heater
options.B: a broken switch that cannot close correctly
options.C: a melted fuse
options.D: a short circuit in the heater

options.A: B gold nucleus gold nucleus

questions.questionText: When a nucleus emits an α-particle, how do the proton number and the nucleon number of the original nucleus change? proton number nucleon number

options.D: +1 no change

questions.questionText: A simple theory of α-particle scattering by a thin metal foil uses the four assumptions given below. Which assumption is exact and is not an approximation?

options.A: Each α-particle interacts with just one nucleus.
options.B: The α-particles lose no kinetic energy when they are deflected.
options.C: The metal nuclei do not recoil.
